# Plan: triage agent, SPE round r01

This is round r01. No `spe/` folder exists yet, so this round also creates it. You asked for local commits after each step. I will commit locally and never push.

Two details were missing, so I chose defaults. The 40 tickets and the support lead's labels will be placed by you at `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` and `spe/evals/data/labels.jsonl`. The pinned reference model is the current Sonnet-class Claude model, and I record its exact ID in `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` when I build it.

## 1. Specify

The spec is your prompt: "triage tickets correctly and cheaply." I will save it verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md`.

### Requirements (r01)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | For each ticket, the agent returns one category from: billing, bug, how-to, account, outage | User: "triage tickets" | `check_schema` |
| R2 | For each ticket, the agent returns one priority from P1, P2, P3, P4 | User: "triage tickets" | `check_schema` |
| R3 | For each ticket, the agent returns a draft first reply | Project brief | `check_schema` (reply is present and not empty) |
| R4 | The category matches the support lead's label | User: "correctly" | `check_category` |
| R5 | The priority matches the support lead's label | User: "correctly" | `check_priority_exact`, `check_priority_within1` |
| R6 | The agent does not under-prioritize true P1 tickets | Decision D3 | `check_p1_recall` |
| R7 | The draft reply addresses the customer's issue and asks for missing details | Decision D4 | `judge_reply` |
| R8 | The draft reply never promises refunds, credits, fixes, or dates, and never invents product facts | Decision D4 | `judge_reply` (hard fail item) |
| R9 | Mean cost per ticket stays at or below $0.01 | User: "cheaply", Decision D2 | `cost_from_usage` |

### Decisions and defaults (`spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Decision | Default I will use | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What "correctly" means | Agreement with the support lead's labels on the 40 tickets | User |
| D2 | What "cheaply" means | Mean cost at or below $0.01 per ticket, computed from token usage | User |
| D3 | Whether missing a P1 is worse than other errors | Yes. I report P1 recall as its own metric. | Support lead |
| D4 | How a reply is graded when no reference replies exist | An LLM judge applies a fixed rubric. The rubric has 4 items. Breaking R8 fails the reply. | Support lead |
| D5 | Whether raw tickets go into git | No. `spe/evals/data/` is gitignored until you confirm the tickets have no customer personal data. | User |
| D6 | Where few-shot examples come from | I write 6 synthetic tickets myself. I take none from the 40 eval tickets, because that would leak answers. | Logged default |

## 2. Predict

### Configurations

Each configuration changes one thing from C0.

| Config | Model | Prompt | Change from C0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| C0 | Pinned Sonnet-class model | Category and priority definitions, JSON output schema | Reference |
| C1 | Pinned Sonnet-class model | C0 prompt plus 6 synthetic examples | Adds few-shot examples |
| C2 | Current Haiku-class model | C0 prompt | Changes the model only |

### Predicted numbers

A hit means the measured value falls inside the band. With 40 tickets, one ticket is 0.025 of accuracy. The bands are wide for that reason.

| Metric | C0 | C1 | C2 | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Schema valid rate | 1.00 ± 0.02 | 1.00 ± 0.02 | 0.98 ± 0.03 | `check_schema` | Structured JSON output rarely breaks. A smaller model breaks it slightly more often. |
| Category accuracy | 0.85 ± 0.07 | 0.88 ± 0.07 | 0.80 ± 0.08 | `check_category` | Most categories are clear from the text. Most misses will be billing versus account and bug versus outage. |
| Priority exact accuracy | 0.65 ± 0.10 | 0.72 ± 0.10 | 0.58 ± 0.10 | `check_priority_exact` | Priority follows the lead's unwritten policy. Examples teach part of that policy. |
| Priority within one level | 0.92 ± 0.06 | 0.94 ± 0.05 | 0.88 ± 0.07 | `check_priority_within1` | Most priority misses will be off by one level, not by two or more. |
| P1 recall | 0.85 ± 0.15 | 0.90 ± 0.15 | 0.75 ± 0.20 | `check_p1_recall` | Outage words make P1 tickets easy to spot. The set likely holds few P1 tickets, so the band is wide. |
| Reply judge pass rate | 0.85 ± 0.08 | 0.87 ± 0.08 | 0.78 ± 0.10 | `judge_reply` | Models tend to offer fixes or credits. R8 will cause most of the failures. |
| Mean cost per ticket (USD) | 0.012 ± 0.004 | 0.016 ± 0.005 | 0.004 ± 0.002 | `cost_from_usage` | Unmeasured estimate. I assume about 2,300 input tokens and 400 output tokens per ticket at list prices. Examples add about 1,200 input tokens. |

My prediction is that C0 and C1 miss R9 and C2 meets it. My prediction is also that C2 loses about 0.05 category accuracy. If that holds, round 2 should test C1's examples on the Haiku-class model.

The naive guess is to label every ticket with the most common category and priority. The control step computes that baseline before launch. I will report it beside the measured numbers.

`spe/predictions/r01.yaml` will set `same_as_last_round: null`, because r01 has no earlier round.

## 3. Evaluate

### Steps after approval

Each step ends with a local commit. The commit message is plain and has no attribution lines.

1. **Scaffold.** Create `spe/` with the transcript, `spec.md`, `disagreements.md`, `README.md`, and a `.gitignore` entry for `spe/evals/data/`. Commit: `spe r01: specify`.
2. **Save the prediction.** Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. The first line will be `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` The author field will read "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode". Commit: `spe r01: predict`.
3. **Build the agent.** Write `triage/prompt.md`, `triage/examples.md` with the 6 synthetic tickets, `triage/schema.json` with fields category, priority, reply, and rationale, and `triage/run.js`. The agent sees only one ticket's text. It has no file tools. Commit: `triage: first agent build`.
4. **Build the graders.** Write the code checks in `spe/evals/harness/graders.js` and the judge rubric in `spe/evals/harness/judge-rubric.md`. Code checks run first. The judge only grades the reply, and it never sees which config wrote the reply. Commit: `spe r01: graders`.
5. **Gate 1: grader selftest.** The oracle uses the lead's labels plus a hand-written good reply, and it must pass every check. An empty output must fail. A wrong output with shifted categories and priorities must fail. If any of these do not happen, I halt and report.
6. **Gate 2: control.** No earlier round exists to regrade. Instead, I grade the majority-class baseline as the control and log that substitution. If the baseline scores above 0.60 on category accuracy, the set is too lopsided and I tell you before launch.
7. **Gate 3: dry run.** Run 3 cells: C0, C1, and C2 on ticket 1, with 1 trial each. I check the schema, the cost logging, and the transcript scan. Commit: `spe r01: gates pass`.
8. **Launch.** Write `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` and start the Workflow. Commit: `spe r01: evaluate`.

### Workflow arguments

| Argument | Value |
|---|---|
| `ROUND` | `"r01"` (the only place the round number appears) |
| `configs` | C0, C1, C2 as defined above |
| `tasks` | 40 tickets from `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` |
| `trials_per_cell` | 3 |
| `split_cell_extra_trials` | Up to 2 more trials, for a cap of 5 per cell, when trials on one cell disagree |
| `judge_model` | Pinned Sonnet-class model, blind to config |
| `budget_cap_usd` | 25. A trial that would cross the cap is skipped and logged. |
| `leak_scan` | Void any trial whose transcript references labels, graders, or predictions |
| `final_steps` | Failure analysis into F-numbered types, then a completeness critic |

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

The run makes 360 base agent calls and up to 240 extra calls on split cells. Agent calls should cost about $3 to $5. The judge grades every reply, which adds about $4 to $6. My total estimate is $8 to $12, under the $25 cap. The dry run will give a real per-call cost. If that cost puts the projection above $25, I will stop and tell you before launch.

## Close-out

The Workflow returns at launch. I close out when its completion notice arrives.

- `spe/prediction-log.md` gets every metric and config with predicted, measured, and verdict. A "Which Why broke" section quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption. It also states whether the naive baseline beat any prediction.
- `spe/failures.md` gets each new failure type, for example billing and account confusion. A grader bug found after the run also counts as a failure, and its original and regraded numbers sit side by side.
- `spec.md` gets a "Proposed for round r02" table. I also write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
- I update `spe/README.md`, commit locally, and tag `spe-r01`.

## Halt conditions

I halt and report to you if the budget cap is reached, if a trial reads the answer key, if a grader is broken, or if a decision in D1 to D5 blocks progress. If every config scores the maximum on a metric, I mark that metric not scorable and propose harder tickets or stricter graders. The loop stops after predictions match results for 3 rounds in a row.
critiques: The plan quotes the prompt as the spec and saves it verbatim. It turns the prompt into requirements R1 to R9 in a table, and each row has a Test column such as `check_category` or `cost_from_usage`.

The 'Predicted numbers' table gives a number with a band for each of C0, C1 and C2. One example is category accuracy of 0.85 ± 0.07, 0.88 ± 0.07 and 0.80 ± 0.08. The table uses numbers, not adjectives.

Every row of the prediction table has a Why column with a reason. One example: 'Priority follows the lead's unwritten policy. Examples teach part of that policy.' The cost row also states its token assumptions.
Step 2 copies the plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`, writes `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`, and commits it as 'spe r01: predict'. That happens before the dry run in step 7 and the launch in step 8.
Gate 1 is a grader selftest with oracle, empty and wrong outputs. Gate 3 is a 3-cell dry run. Both run before step 8 starts the Workflow defined in `r01-workflow.js`.
The prediction table has a 'Grader check' column. It ties each metric to a named check, such as `check_p1_recall` for P1 recall and `judge_reply` for the reply pass rate.

The Close-out section writes `spe/prediction-log.md` with predicted, measured and verdict for each metric, plus a 'Which Why broke' section. It seeds the next round with a 'Proposed for round r02' table and `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml`.
